title: Stock Market Update: Positive-Sounding Trade Headlines Lift Stocks
text:
Positive-Sounding Trade Headlines Lift Stocks 12-Dec-18 13:00 ET Dow +413.21 at 24783.45, Nasdaq +155.44 at 7187.27, S&P +45.18 at 2681.96
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has climbed 1.6% amid hope that conciliatory trade developments will help produce a meaningful trade deal between the U.S. and China.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (+1.6%), the Nasdaq Composite (+2.1%), and the Russell 2000 (+1.7%) also trade higher in a session that has lacked the roller-coaster action seen of late. The major indices opened notably higher, underpinned by positive-sounding trade headlines, and have continued to draw a bid. They are currently sitting at, or near, their highs for the day.
President Trump provided some uplifting rhetoric in a Reuters interview, saying Ms. Meng was granted bail Tuesday by a Vancouver court.
In addition, a Wall Street Journal report indicated that China is looking companies. The revised plan could roll out early next year when trade negotiations between the two counties are expected to accelerate before the March 1 deadline.
These occurrences have fueled renewed should bode well for economic growth prospects.
The foundation for today's rally has been underpinned by some solid leadership from the S&P 500 information technology (+2.1%), consumer discretionary (+2.1%), health care (+2.0%), and communication services (+1.9%) sectors.
Chip stocks, and an upside bias in shares of Apple (AAPL 170.88, +2.50, +1.3%), have provided the heavily-weighted tech sector strong support. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is up 2.6%.
Something equally important is that the S&P 500 financial sector (+1.5%) -- which is a key driver of economic sentiment -- has started to get on board with things, which was questionable earlier in the day. This is an important development as a stronger showing from the beaten-up financial sector should help perpetuate the belief that the market, absent some nettlesome headline, is due for a decent-sized bounce.
Given the market's rally effort, the defensive-oriented utilities (-0.4%) and real estate (-1.4%) sectors have underperformed today. The consumer staples group is also underperforming with a slim gain of 0.2%.
U.S. Treasuries have also edged lower, pushing yields higher, amid the stock market rally. The benchmark 10-yr yield is up three basis points to 2.90%. Meanwhile, the U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.4% to 97.05.
Separately, there has been a good bit of attention paid today to the UK where a "no confidence" vote is being held by the Conservative Party with respect to Prime Minister's May's leadership. The vote comes plan, yet reports indicate Ms. May is likely to survive the vote.
